description: The committed authoritative shared-responsibility key for module 20 (cloud-shared-responsibility), MAP mode. The cited matrix IS the oracle: there is no byte parser and no authored per-render answer — `mapping_correct` reads each card's placement against the cited keyByModel/keyZone derived from the AWS Shared Responsibility Model + CSA Consensus Assessments matrix + NIST 800-53 control families. The IaaS/PaaS/SaaS slider re-derives placement so a card visibly migrates across the you/provider boundary as the service model changes (the boundary is a movable line).

provenance.authored_from: AWS Shared Responsibility Model (aws.amazon.com/compliance/shared-responsibility-model) + Cloud Security Alliance Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ) shared-responsibility columns + NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 control families (SC-12/SC-28 cryptographic protection, CM-6/CM-7 configuration, SA-22/SI-2 flaw remediation, AC-2/AC-3/IA-2 access enforcement, PE-* physical, AU-2/AU-6/AU-12 audit) + AICPA SOC 2 TSC CUEC guidance (complementary user-entity controls). Vendor-neutral control-plane/data-plane split per the CSA / NIST SP 800-204 distinction between the management API surface and the workload traffic surface.
provenance.honesty_note: Every zone assignment carries a keyRef citation to its authoritative source. No value is read off a wire — this is a conceptual module: the cited matrix is the closed answer key the verifier compares placements against. The slider re-derivation (keyByModel) reproduces the published shift of responsibility from IaaS to SaaS, where the customer's surface shrinks as the provider's managed surface grows; the constant cards (customer data, IAM access) reproduce the model's invariant that managing your own data and who reaches it is yours under every model ('security IN the cloud').

items.label: Physical facilities, hardware, and the host hypervisor
items.keyRef: AWS SRM 'security OF the cloud' (PE-* physical/environmental); provider-owned at every model

items.label: Guest-OS patching and flaw remediation
items.keyRef: AWS SRM guest-OS patching (SA-22/SI-2): customer under IaaS, managed by provider once the OS is abstracted (PaaS/SaaS)

items.label: Application code and its runtime configuration
items.keyRef: AWS SRM application layer (SA-* / CM-6): customer-owned on IaaS/PaaS, provider-owned application in SaaS

items.label: Network and firewall (security-group) configuration
items.keyRef: AWS SRM network traffic protection / configuration (CM-7/SC-7): customer-configured on IaaS/PaaS, provider-managed in SaaS

items.label: Encryption at rest (the storage setting + key custody)
items.keyRef: AWS SRM client-/server-side encryption (SC-12/SC-28): customer enables it and may hold the key on IaaS/PaaS; in SaaS the provider attests it and the customer INHERITS the control via a CUEC (SOC 2 complementary user-entity control)

items.label: Customer data: what it is and who may read it
items.keyRef: AWS SRM 'security IN the cloud' — customer data + identity/access management (AC-2/AC-3): always the customer's, at every model

items.label: Creating an IAM role / changing a resource policy
items.keyRef: CSA / NIST SP 800-204 control plane: identity and policy administration is a management-API action (AC-2/AC-3 enforcement is configured here)

items.label: Editing a security-group / firewall rule
items.keyRef: CSA control plane: a firewall rule change is a management-API configuration action (CM-7), not workload traffic

items.label: Rotating a KMS encryption key
items.keyRef: CSA control plane: key lifecycle administration is a management-API action (SC-12); the key's USE on a payload is data-plane

items.label: An application reading/writing objects in a bucket
items.keyRef: NIST SP 800-204 data plane: serving the workload's request/response traffic and the bytes it moves

items.label: User request traffic hitting the running workload
items.keyRef: NIST SP 800-204 data plane: live request/response traffic to the workload

items.label: Audit logging that evidences both planes
items.keyRef: AU-2/AU-12 audit: management-API actions (control-plane events) AND data-access events (data-plane events) both produce audit evidence — a THROUGHOUT control spanning both planes (e.g. CloudTrail management + data events)
